title: decree events.jsonl line
description: One line of a run's .decree/runs/<id>/events.jsonl (JSON Lines): one event, a JSON object. The file is both the run's record and its telemetry, written to be shipped to a log store as it is. Every event carries the common fields, so each line stands alone in a log pipeline, plus the fields of its `type`. The schema lists every field decree 0.5 writes and allows no other, so decree's own tests catch an undocumented field; within v1 new optional fields and new types may still be added (docs/reference/README.md, Versioning), so a consumer should ignore fields and types it does not know. Reference: docs/reference/runs.md, events.jsonl.

v.description: Schema version, 1. Added fields do not bump it; renamed or removed fields do.

ts.description: When the event was written: RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds.

type.description: The kind of event, which decides its other fields: `transition`, `script`, `decision`, `waiting`, `received`, `run_finished` or `interrupted`.

run_id.description: The message `id`: the run's folder, runs/<id>/.

trigger.description: The message's `trigger`: how the run started.

trace_id.description: The run's W3C Trace Context trace id: from the message's `traceparent` if valid, else random. A child run shares its parent's. Its spans are in runs/<id>/traces.jsonl (docs/reference/observability.md, Traces).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds, such as 2026-10-01T14:30:05.123Z.

traceId.description: A W3C Trace Context trace id: 32 lowercase hex digits, not all zeros.

spanId.description: A W3C Trace Context span id: 16 lowercase hex digits, not all zeros.

transition.title: transition
transition.description: The state changed (or an attempt was recorded). The only type that state, status and visits are derived from.

from.description: Atomic state left. `null` on the claim and `invalid_message` events.

event.description: Event taken. `claimed` on the claim event.

source.description: Where the event came from. `claim`: the claim event. `exit_code`: `done`/`error` from the exit code (or a pass-through `done`). `script`: an event the script named in $DECREE_EVENT_FILE. `attempt`: a failed attempt that will be re-run, with `from` and `to` equal. `check`, `model`, `person`: decision invokes. `machine`: the final state of a child run from a `machine` invoke (`failed` as `error`), and also `error` when no child could start. `timeout`: a `person` deadline. `internal`: a `done.state.<id>` event decree raised. `invalid_message`: a message rejected at claim. `retry`: written by `decree retry`.

exit_code.description: The invoke's exit code. `null` if there was no invoke.

invalid_event.description: The undeclared event the invoke named (docs/reference/scripts.md, Events from an invoke, step 4); the event is then `error`.

exit_failures.description: Names of the `onexit` scripts that failed on this transition.

file.description: On a claim from the inbox or migrations: the original filename. Absent for a child run (trigger `invoke`), which has no file.

error.description: On an `invalid_message` event, the validation message; on a `machine` invoke that could not start, why the child did not start.

span_id.description: On the claim (`claim` or `invalid_message`) and on a `retry` event: the run span it starts.

parent_span_id.description: On the claim, when the message's `traceparent` names a parent: the run span's parent span (an invoking state's span for a child run, a script's span for an emitted message).

script.title: script
script.description: One script execution finished. Written after the script exits, before any `transition` it causes.

state.description: State the script ran for, or `_root`.

path.description: File that ran, relative to the project root.

started_at.description: When the script started: RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds.

exit_code.description: The script's exit code. `null` if killed by a signal.

timed_out.description: Present only when the script timed out, and then always `true`.

log.description: Log filename in the run folder.

span_id.description: The script's span, which its TRACEPARENT named.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: A `check`, `model` or `person` invoke produced its event. Written before the `transition` it causes.

span_id.description: The decision's span. For a `model` decision, the parent of the router run's run span.

checkDecision.title: check decision
checkDecision.description: A `check` evaluated its condition; the event is `true` or `false`.

condition.description: The condition as written in the machine.

modelDecision.title: model decision
modelDecision.description: A router answered a `model` request, or failed to. The event is the pick, `unsure` below `min_confidence`, or `error` with `router_error`.

options.description: The options offered, in name order.

child_run.description: The router's child run id. Absent when `max_depth` stopped it from starting.

pick.description: The model's pick, even when the event is `unsure`. Absent when the event is `error`.

reason.description: Reason from the reply, if given.

confidence.description: Confidence from the reply, 0 to 1, if reported.

probabilities.description: A number per option, if reported.

router_error.description: When the event is `error`: why there is no pick. The reply was rejected (and why), the router run failed, or `max_depth <n> reached`.

duration_ms.description: Wall time of the router run, in milliseconds; 0 when none started.

personDecision.title: person decision
personDecision.description: A person's reply was delivered to a `person` state.

options.description: The options offered, in name order.

waiting.title: waiting
waiting.description: The run is paused: in a `person` state for a reply, or in a `machine` or `model` state for its child run.

personWait.title: person wait
personWait.description: Waiting in a `person` state for a reply.

wait_id.description: <run id>.w<seq>; a reply must name it (or the run id).

timeout_at.description: RFC 3339 deadline from the `person` invoke's `timeout`, or `null` without one.

childWait.title: child wait
childWait.description: Waiting in a `machine` or `model` state for its child run.

child.description: The child run waited for (a sub-machine or a router).

received.title: received
received.description: An external event arrived for a waiting run: a reply, a timeout, or a finished child run.

span_id.description: The wait's span, from the `waiting` event to this one. For a `machine` invoke, the parent of the child run's run span.

timeoutReceived.title: timeout received
timeoutReceived.description: A `person` wait passed its deadline; the event is `error`.

childReceived.title: child received
childReceived.description: The child run waited for finished.

child.description: The child run's id; `event` is its final state (`failed` as `error`).

run_finished.title: run_finished
run_finished.description: The run reached a root-level final state and root `onexit` has run. Always the run's last event, unless `decree retry` continues it.

duration_ms.description: From the claim event to now, in milliseconds; 0 for a message rejected at claim.

interrupted.title: interrupted
interrupted.description: The run stopped before a final state.

cause.description: `signal` (SIGINT or SIGTERM) or `crash` (found later with a stale or missing lock).

script.description: Script that was running, if known.
